content.title: Why does Easter fall on different dates every year? Here's why
content.text: NEWSWhy does Easter fall on different dates every year? Here's what determines the day Victoria E. FreileNew York Connect TeamApril 4, 2026, 10:52 a.m. ETKeep Watching7Easter Sunday falls on April 5 in 2026 in the Western Christian calendar. In the Eastern Orthodox tradition, where the holiday is known as Pascha, it will be observed on April 12.Why does Easter change every year?Easter does not have a fixed date because it is tied to both the solar and lunar calendars. In Western Christianity, Easter is celebrated on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the spring equinox (March 21).Because the timing of the full moon varies each year, Easter can fall anywhere between March 22 and April 25.Eastern Orthodox churches use a different method based on the Julian calendar, which is why their Easter is often celebrated on a later date.Key Easter-related dates in 2026Palm Sunday: March 29Holy Thursday (Maundy Thursday): April 2Good Friday: April 3Easter Sunday: April 5What is Easter?Easter is one of the most important holidays in Christianity, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
